tool.name: RelocateGeodatabase

param.name: in_gdb
param.dialogReference:
The file geodatabase holding the data to relocate, for example a geodatabase of Thailand.

Every feature class, feature dataset, raster, and table it contains is listed in Datasets to Relocate.
param.pythonReference:
The file geodatabase holding the data to relocate, for example a geodatabase of Thailand.

Every feature class, feature dataset, raster, and table it contains is listed in Datasets to Relocate.

param.name: samples_fc
param.dialogReference:
A point feature class with the source and destination points. Defaults to the feature class named 'samples' in the input geodatabase.

Example: one point on Bangkok (source) and one on Pikes Peak (destination).
param.pythonReference:
A point feature class with the source and destination points. Defaults to the feature class named 'samples' in the input geodatabase.

Example: one point on Bangkok (source) and one on Pikes Peak (destination).

param.name: id_field
param.dialogReference:
The field whose values identify each sample point. A field named role, type, name, label, or id is chosen automatically if one exists; otherwise ObjectID is used.

Values must be unique.
param.pythonReference:
The field whose values identify each sample point. A field named role, type, name, label, or id is chosen automatically if one exists; otherwise ObjectID is used.

Values must be unique.

param.name: source_point
param.dialogReference:
The sample point that acts as the origin. Data keeps true distance and bearing from this point after it is moved.

In the Thailand example, choose the Bangkok point.
param.pythonReference:
The sample point that acts as the origin. Data keeps true distance and bearing from this point after it is moved.

In the Thailand example, choose the Bangkok point.

param.name: destination_point
param.dialogReference:
The sample point where the source point will land. All data moves with it.

In the Thailand example, choose the Pikes Peak point.
param.pythonReference:
The sample point where the source point will land. All data moves with it.

In the Thailand example, choose the Pikes Peak point.

param.name: out_folder
param.dialogReference: The folder where the new file geodatabase is created. Defaults to the folder holding the input geodatabase.
param.pythonReference: The folder where the new file geodatabase is created. Defaults to the folder holding the input geodatabase.

param.name: out_name
param.dialogReference:
The name of the new file geodatabase. Defaults to the input name with _relocated added. .gdb is appended if missing.

The tool will not overwrite an existing geodatabase unless overwriting outputs is enabled.
param.pythonReference:
The name of the new file geodatabase. Defaults to the input name with _relocated added. .gdb is appended if missing.

The tool will not overwrite an existing geodatabase unless overwriting outputs is enabled.

param.name: out_coor_system
param.dialogReference:
The coordinate system of the relocated data. Defaults to the WGS 1984 UTM zone that contains the destination point (UTM zone 13N for Pikes Peak).

Choose any coordinate system that suits the destination area.
param.pythonReference:
The coordinate system of the relocated data. Defaults to the WGS 1984 UTM zone that contains the destination point (UTM zone 13N for Pikes Peak).

Choose any coordinate system that suits the destination area.

param.name: datasets
param.dialogReference:
The feature classes, rasters, and tables to copy into the output geodatabase. All are checked by default except the samples feature class.

Feature classes and rasters are moved and reprojected. Tables have no location and are copied unchanged.
param.pythonReference:
The feature classes, rasters, and tables to copy into the output geodatabase. All are checked by default except the samples feature class.

Feature classes and rasters are moved and reprojected. Tables have no location and are copied unchanged.

param.name: resampling_type
param.dialogReference:
How raster cell values are resampled during reprojection.

AUTO (default): NEAREST for integer rasters such as land cover, BILINEAR for floating-point rasters such as elevation.

NEAREST: keeps original values; use for categorical data. BILINEAR or CUBIC: smooth interpolation for continuous data. MAJORITY: most common value in the neighborhood; for categorical data.
param.pythonReference:
How raster cell values are resampled during reprojection.

AUTO (default): NEAREST for integer rasters such as land cover, BILINEAR for floating-point rasters such as elevation.

NEAREST: keeps original values; use for categorical data. BILINEAR or CUBIC: smooth interpolation for continuous data. MAJORITY: most common value in the neighborhood; for categorical data.

param.name: cell_size
param.dialogReference:
The output raster cell size, in the linear units of the output coordinate system.

Leave blank to keep each raster's native ground resolution.
param.pythonReference:
The output raster cell size, in the linear units of the output coordinate system.

Leave blank to keep each raster's native ground resolution.

param.name: max_deviation
param.dialogReference:
How far a reprojected line or polygon edge may stray from its true curved path before extra vertices are added. Smaller values keep shapes more exact but create larger files.

Default is 10 meters.
param.pythonReference:
How far a reprojected line or polygon edge may stray from its true curved path before extra vertices are added. Smaller values keep shapes more exact but create larger files.

Default is 10 meters.

param.name: out_gdb
param.dialogReference: The new file geodatabase holding the relocated data and a RELOCATION_INFO table describing the run.
param.pythonReference: The new file geodatabase holding the relocated data and a RELOCATION_INFO table describing the run.

tool.summary: Copies the data in a file geodatabase into a new file geodatabase and moves it so the source sample point lands on the destination sample point, keeping true ground size, shape, and orientation.
tool.usage:
The samples feature class must contain at least two points with unique identifier values: the source (origin) and the destination.

Each dataset is projected into an Azimuthal Equidistant projection centered on the source point, relabeled as Azimuthal Equidistant centered on the destination point, then projected into the output coordinate system.

Distances and bearings from the source point are exact. Distortion grows slowly with distance; datasets reaching more than 2,500 km from the source point produce a warning.

Rasters are resampled twice (into and out of the intermediate projection). Use NEAREST or MAJORITY for categorical rasters.

Simple feature classes, raster datasets, and tables are supported. Annotation, dimension, mosaic datasets, topologies, networks, and relationship classes are skipped with a warning.

Attribute values are not changed. Elevation values in a relocated DEM still describe the original terrain.

The output geodatabase includes a RELOCATION_INFO table recording the points, coordinate systems, and settings used.
